# Lexicographically Smallest Palindrome.

@example Only the two middle letters, b and d, disagree. One edit is enough, and writing b over the d gives the earlier string.
"kibdik"
=> "kibbik"

@example p faces r and e faces a, so two edits are needed; keeping the earlier letter of each pair gives paap.
"pear"
=> "paap"

@example Already a palindrome, so no edit may be made, even though "aka" would come earlier.
"tkt"
=> "tkt"

# A single letter is a palindrome on its own.
"a"
=> "a"

# Two different letters: both become the earlier one, on whichever side it is.
"zy"
=> "yy"

"by"
=> "bb"

# Pairs that disagree in both directions, none of them holding an a.
"fdkcrg"
=> "fdccdf"

# Odd length: the middle x and the matched h's stay; only p and w meet.
"hpxwh"
=> "hpxph"

# Only the outermost pair disagrees.
"zbccby"
=> "ybccby"

# Only the innermost pair disagrees: two neighbours in an even length, and
# the pair around the middle letter in an odd one.
"mnoqnm"
=> "mnoonm"

"rstuvsr"
=> "rstutsr"

# The ends of the alphabet: a against z in both directions.
"zaza"
=> "aaaa"

# An even-length palindrome with no a stays as it is.
"qwwq"
=> "qwwq"

# Every pair disagrees, odd length.
"zyxwvutsrqpon"
=> "nopqrstsrqpon"

# 1000 letters, one more than a 1000-byte buffer holds with its NUL: the
# left half is dy repeated, the right half bz repeated, so the pairs are
# d with z and y with b, in turn.
""
=> ""

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"bbababb"
=> "bbababb"

@gen 4 small
"mnom"
=> "mnnm"

@gen 5 small
"baacab"
=> "baaaab"

@gen 7 small
"zyzyzy"
=> "yyyyyy"

@gen 8 small
"acccaac"
=> "aaacaaa"

@gen 10 small
"aaaabbbb"
=> "aaaaaaaa"

@gen 13 small
"xzzyz"
=> "xyzyx"

@gen 15 small
"jyamtmjt"
=> "jjammajj"

# Full size: 999 or 1000 letters, with no pair, about seven in ten pairs,
# and every pair disagreeing.
@gen 2
""
=> ""

@gen 3
""
=> ""

@gen 8
""
=> ""
